stem: Explain the importance of mitosis in crop production.

stem: A farmer says: "Buying an expensive bull with excellent genes is all I need to improve my herd." Evaluate this statement using your knowledge of genes, cell division and the environment.

points.description: The bull passes on genes through sperm made by meiosis, each carrying half his chromosomes.
Each calf gets half its genes from the cow, so cows' quality matters too.
Meiosis gives variation, so not every calf inherits the best combination of genes.
Calves grow by mitosis, but their growth depends on feeding, water and health (environment).
Poor nutrition, disease or ticks prevent good genes from being expressed.
Judgement: a good bull helps but improvement needs good cows, selection of offspring and good management.

levels.descriptor: Accurate, well-developed explanation of several relevant points using correct agricultural terms, applied to the crop, animal or situation in the question, with a clear judgement where one is asked for.
Some relevant points explained, partly developed or only partly applied to the situation; any judgement is simple or one-sided.
Simple statements or a list of points with little explanation or application.

answerSpec.modelAnswer: A good bull does improve a herd, because his sperm, made by meiosis, carry his genes for growth into many calves. But each sperm carries only half of his chromosomes, and each calf receives the other half from its dam, so the cows also matter. Because meiosis shuffles genes, the calves vary and not all inherit his best qualities, so the farmer must still select the best offspring. Finally, genes only set potential: calves that are underfed, short of water or carrying heavy tick and worm loads will not grow well. So the statement is too simple: the bull is one part of improvement, together with good cows, selection and good management.

explanation: Weigh genetic and environmental factors and judge.
hints: What does meiosis do to the bull's genes in his offspring?
